payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Context
The vault migration must preserve valid tracker state while publishing canonical redacted events.
This record ships with basicly-gtb19bg.43.39 and basicly-gtb19bg.43.40 as cut B.
## Decisions
The Orchestrator decision of 2026-11-13 supersedes literal event-id preservation when payloads require changes. This is amendment C6.
Every record id remains unchanged. Unchanged payloads retain their event ids. Changed payloads receive valid deterministic ids.
F1 defines one-time import. After cutover, the redacted vault is authoritative. Normal operation never depends on a private map.
Determinism compares canonical ledger bytes and event ids. Git commit hashes depend on destination parents and are excluded.
F2 keeps old-to-new id mapping private, optional, and at an explicitly supplied path. There is no default repository location.
Resolve mapping paths before checking them. Paths outside every Git checkout are allowed.
Inside another checkout, Git must confirm that the destination is ignored.
Vault checkouts and their worktrees are always refused, even when ignored.
Create owner-readable mapping files where supported. Existing mappings require an explicit overwrite flag.
Ignore files are never edited. Mapping contents and unredacted hashes never reach shared output.
Mapping entries identify changed fields and account for removed events. They contain no plaintext removed value.
A control proved that an old event id can confirm a hidden holder name from a short candidate list.
Preserve valid reviews and closed state. Never promote stale or invalid evidence. Preserve operational event references and account for history.
Report external event-id citations without rewriting commit history, changelog or documentation.
The reviewed prototype commits are 49afcf1d and cf70d665. Replace their invalid id preservation and view normalization.
The original source ledger remains untouched. Live cutover and release remain outside this build.
## Demonstration
python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py migrate --to-vault --preview reports canonical counts and digest without writes.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
When a ledger is imported, every record id and every unchanged event id shall be preserved.
Changed payloads shall receive valid deterministic event ids, and the unchanged kit fsck shall accept the canonical result.
Two independent imports of identical input shall produce identical canonical bytes and ids, including rehearsal and cutover.
Source fixtures shall prove imports from beads, br and beans without losing record identities.
A prefix export shall preserve the canonical event count and fold of the vault view.
If counts or digests differ, migration shall refuse before publication and name both public values.
Migration shall report redacted and re-minted counts and changed field names without exposing private hashes or old ids.
Valid review, confirmation and closed state shall survive migration; stale or invalid evidence shall never become current.
Every source event shall be accounted for, operational event references shall resolve, and projected sequences shall be gapless.
Private mapping shall use an explicit resolved private destination, remain optional, and never reach shared output or logs.
Repeated import of the same source into the same vault shall refuse without writing.
Preview of a ledger import shall report canonical counts and digest without changing files or fetching.
Ledger imports shall read every source event from trunk and pending logs, preserving fold order and record identities.
Each import batch commit shall append at most 1 MiB, and each segment shall remain within that bound.

payload.text: Verified 2026-11-13 against https://git-scm.com/docs/git-check-ignore and https://git-scm.com/docs/git-rev-parse with Git 2.55.0. Quiet check-ignore returns 0 for ignored paths and 1 for tracked or unignored paths. It does not report tracked files by default. The installed controls returned 0 for .venv and node_modules probes, and 1 for AGENTS.md. The initial .basicly/usage probe also returned 1; it established no ignored-path guarantee. The absolute git-common-dir probe returned an existing absolute directory. The private-path rule follows the accepted Orchestrator clarification of 2026-11-13. No fetched vendor document was stored.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When a configured repository holds a vault-born record, create, update, close, comment, review, confirm and dependency writes shall validate against the vault view and queue the intended ledger events with no local ledger event write.
- When the engine or standalone CLI performs those writes, both shall call one adapter and preserve readiness, confirmation, field, dependency and holder checks.
- When the standalone tracker is installed without the harness, init, create, claim, update, review, confirm, close and read against a local bare vault shall complete with no local ledger event writes.
- When a command is invalid or a record is absent, it shall refuse by the real cause without writing an event.
payload.description:
## Context
When a record is created after a repository switches to the vault, I want to create, update, review, confirm, link and close it through ordinary tracker commands, so I can complete work without a writable local ledger.
The closed V3 record basicly-gtb19bg.43.28 criterion 1 promises these writes, but commands._require and vault_write._refused validate against local events before vault_write.land reads the vault view; src/basicly/owned_write.py also requires the local record. Native vault handlers currently cover comment, claim and unassign, leaving the general lifecycle unavailable for vault-born records.
## Scope
One shared adapter validates against the vault view and queues carried ledger events without local ledger writes; engine and standalone commands use that adapter. Preserve existing write gates and ownership rules. Cut C2 starts from main after cut B normalization lands.
## Evidence
The .43.28 confirmation recorded 16 passing tests in tests/test_kit_vault_write.py; its WRITES parameterization uses _seeded local records, while the create test does not perform a subsequent write on the created id. The observed missing-local rejection is tracked by basicly-ak6qrz0. Cut D and E cover migration and cutover rather than implementation of this missing lifecycle.
payload.title: Repair the complete write lifecycle for vault-born records

payload.acceptance_criteria: When the retrospective examines the V3 confirmation and tests, it shall identify the accepted check, demonstrate the missing vault-born lifecycle input and propose a concrete control without changing gates.
payload.description:
## Context
When a closed record has an unmet lifecycle criterion, I want to identify the check that accepted it and the input it never exercised, so I can improve later review without inventing passing evidence.
The closed basicly-gtb19bg.43.28 criterion 1 promised create, update, close, comment, review, confirm and dependency writes through the vault. Its confirmation cites 16 passing tests in tests/test_kit_vault_write.py. The write parameterization constructs local records through _seeded; the separate create test checks queueing but never writes to that vault-born id. commands._require and vault_write._refused still require local events; basicly-ak6qrz0 records the consumer failure.
## Scope
Retrospective input only: establish the accepted check and missing consumer sequence, then propose a control; no gate changes or closure bypass.
payload.title: Explain why vault write closure missed the vault-born lifecycle
